questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose the University of Oslo because it offered English courses relevant to my home program. I also chose Norway because of the nature.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The courses were interesting!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy, the University of Oslo had clear information and steps to follow on the website.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got a lot of emails upon arrival with all the information I needed, and also had the opportunity to participate in an online intro-meeting.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I found hosing through
finn.no
- it can be hard to find housing on your own, but I wrote to a lot of people and got lucky, so I would recommend you do the same. But the university also offers housing through Sio, which is very nice and convenient!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I lived in the city centre, which was a nice experience. And it is easy to get to the university (Blindern) from anywhere :)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I lived at Vulkan near Grunerløkka

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Course registration opens early, and if you just apply straight away it is pretty sure you get the courses you want.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You apply thourgh studentweb. You find english courses in the course cataloug (check if you are eligeble for the courses before!)

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I contacted the student information once before registration; they are there to help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Succesfull - I got into all the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Check beforehand if your are eligble. And don't worry to much, it will work out!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took master's-level courses; they were somewhat easy to follow. A lot of assignments and projects throughout the semester, but overall okey.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More projects and presentations. But it was similar to class-style teaching.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
RSNE4100
Cultural-historical and decolonial approaches to learning, development, and inclusion

SPED4403
Special topics in specific learning difficulties

SPED4603
Neurodevelopmental disorders in a lifespan perspective

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
This course was very interesting, and the exam was early in the semester - which was nice: RSNE4100
Cultural-historical and decolonial approaches to learning, development, and inclusion

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Traveling... Spent money on travelling to cabins and other cities! Good to budget for! The gym membership as well (270)!

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries were even more expensive than I expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They have many clubs and sports to join as an exchange student. I would recommend joining group dance classes (I didn't do it, but a friend of mine did, it looked very fun)

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: SiO student gym membership.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend signing up for the gym membership. It's affordable; you can use all the gyms around the city, you can join many group training sessions, and you have access to the swimming pool.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to Bergen for a weekend trip! Take the train, it's a beautiful train ride! And go to the islands outside Oslo.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy, it isn't that much different to the Danish culture. Just remember that the shops are closed on sundays.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join a club, maybe - but I mostly hung out with other internationals.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
That the shops were closed on Sundays - you have to organize you're grocery shopping a little better. 
And the Norwegians are very introverted, which is also something to get used to (but very friendly when you get to know them).

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The quietness of Oslo! And how active people are. Always running, skiing or going on hikes.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Enjoy the nature! Go on hikes! 

Make an effort to meet people; the people make the stay special.

Go travelling, but also enjoy Oslo city!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be up to date with all the information you get from the host university and Mobility online - it makes everything easier!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people and making friends from all around Europe :)

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Maybe taking the courses in English and taking courses that I was maybe totally not prepared for. It took some getting used to.. But everything works out!

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Enjoy Oslo!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
